audit.primary_source_citation: Picant V, Revol-Bauz L, Tonon L, Casini T, Voissière A, Poujol D, Picard E, Rodriguez C, Degletagne C, Sible E, Hasan U, Ferrari A, Caux C, Bendriss-Vermare N. "Interleukin-35 impairs human NK cell effector functions and induces their ILC1-like conversion with tissue residency features." Nat Commun. 2025 Jul 3;16:4782. PMID 40610398; PMCID PMC12229632; DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-61196-0. Preprint: Res Sq 10.21203/rs.3.rs-4030216/v1 (2024). CITATION VERIFIED — the hinted paper exists, Picant is first author, journal/year correct. This is the first and only primary source for the IL-35-specific version of the claim. Archived: /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC12229632.txt
audit.species: Human (Homo sapiens). Peripheral blood from anonymous healthy French volunteer donors, Etablissement Français du Sang Lyon, convention 16-093. No animals used anywhere in the paper.
audit.what_was_measured: In human PBMC-derived NK cells (negatively selected, purity >90%; or FACS-sorted CD56+CD3-NKG2C+ vs NKG2C-, purity >98%), cultured in vitro in RPMI + 20% human AB serum + IL-2 (100 IU/mL) with or without recombinant IL-35 (PeproTech 200-37, 100 ng/mL, medium renewed every 2 days), at days 2, 4 and 8, surface expression of CD9, CD103 (ITGAE) and CD49a (ITGA1) was measured by spectral flow cytometry (Cytek Aurora / LSRFortessa) alongside intracellular EOMES, T-BET and IFN-γ, in 3 individual donors (Fig 5a, 5d), 5 donors (Fig 5f) and 3-6 donors (Fig 6f, TGF-β blockade); in parallel, 10x Genomics 3' v3.1 scRNA-seq with CellPlex CMO condition-hashing was run at days 2 and 4 on 2 donors (~5,000 cells per condition) and an "ILC1-like" UCell gene-signature score was computed per cell. Readout is the population frequency of CD9+CD103+CD49a+ events per well, compared paired within donor against the IL-2-alone arm — not any per-cell or per-clone tracking of a given NK cell acquiring the phenotype.
audit.n: 3 donors for the core CD9/CD103/CD49a conversion kinetics (Fig 5a, 5d); 5 donors (Fig 5f); 3-6 donors for the TGF-β-blockade rescue (Fig 6f); 2 donors for scRNA-seq. Largest n supporting the marker claim = 5.
audit.n_unit: healthy human blood donors (biological replicates); NOT cells. The 354,379-cell / 108-patient-sample figures elsewhere in the paper are in-silico re-analysis of four public tumour scRNA-seq datasets (GSE131907, GSE160269, GSE166555, GSE176078), not experimental n for this claim.
audit.controls: Paired same-donor IL-2-alone arm (paired t-test) for every conversion timepoint. Viability/survival control: NK survival statistically identical ±IL-35 out to day 9, so reduced cell number is not selective death. CTV proliferation assay: IL-35 significantly REDUCES proliferation. Purity controls: bulk NK >90%, FACS-sorted NKG2C+ and NKG2C- each >98%, and both sorted subsets converted. Mechanistic controls: anti-TGF-β1/2/3 (R&D MAB1835) vs mouse IgG1 isotype (MAB002), and Galunisertib (TGF-βR inhibitor) vs DMSO vehicle, both of which prevented acquisition of CD9/CD103/CD49a. TGF-β alone (1 ng/mL) used as positive control for conversion. IL-35 washout/starvation arm (3 washes + 48 h) to test reversibility. MISSING control: the starting population was never sorted or gated to be CD9-CD103-CD49a-, so a pre-existing tissue-residency-marker-positive fraction is not formally excluded at t=0; and the bulk >90% purity leaves up to ~10% non-NK contaminants in the non-sorted experiments.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Selection/outgrowth of a pre-existing CD9+CD103+CD49a+ subset, plus a culture artefact of supraphysiological cytokine exposure. The paper argues against pure selection reasonably well but not decisively: IL-35 SUPPRESSES proliferation and does not alter survival, so neither preferential expansion nor preferential death of the CD49a- majority is an easy explanation, and "nearly all cells" are marker-positive by day 8, which is arithmetically hard to reach by selecting a near-absent blood precursor without proliferation; both >98%-pure NKG2C+ and NKG2C- sorted subsets converted, so it is not one contaminating subset. What remains genuinely unexcluded: (1) no clonal or per-cell tracking exists — the CellPlex CMO barcoding is SAMPLE/CONDITION hashing, not lineage barcoding, so no individual NK cell was ever observed to acquire the phenotype; the entire claim rests on population-frequency shifts between wells; (2) t=0 was never sorted CD9-CD103-CD49a-; (3) the phenotype is defined by three integrins/tetraspanin plus a signature score, and TGF-β is long known to induce exactly these markers on cultured blood NK cells, so "ILC1-like conversion" may be a reversible TGF-β-driven phenotypic state rather than a lineage change (EOMES fell but T-BET was unchanged — an incomplete ILC1 transcription-factor switch); (4) reagent artefact — see counter_evidence.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, three strands. (1) REAGENT VALIDITY: Aparicio-Siegmund et al., PLoS One 2014;9(9):e107990, PMID 25259790, "Recombinant p35 from Bacteria Can Form Interleukin (IL-)12, but Not IL-35" — reconstituted recombinant IL-35 failed to induce STAT1/STAT3 phosphorylation and failed to induce proliferation of Ba/F3-gp130-IL-12Rβ1-IL-12Rβ2 cells; the authors "fail to create IL-35 by this approach". Partial mitigation: PeproTech 200-37 as used here is a HEK293-expressed 406-aa single-chain IL-12A-EBI3 fusion (~45.8 kDa), not a bacterial reconstitution — but it is still a non-native single-chain construct used at 100 ng/mL, a high dose, and the field-wide reagent caveat is unresolved. (2) MECHANISTIC DISPLACEMENT — the strongest counter to the claim AS WORDED: the paper's own data show conversion is mediated by AUTOCRINE TGF-β, is completely abrogated by anti-TGF-β1/2/3 or Galunisertib, and is reproduced by TGF-β alone. The pre-existing primary literature already established TGF-β-driven NK→CD49a+CD103+CD9+ ILC1-like conversion (Gao et al., Nat Immunol 2017, PMID 28759001, mouse, with genetic fate mapping; Cortez et al. 2016, PMID 27156386). So IL-35 is an upstream inducer of TGF-β, not the differentiation signal itself; "IL-35 drives NK toward an ILC1-like phenotype" is one causal step removed from what was measured. (3) NO INDEPENDENT REPLICATION of the conversion: the only independent IL-35/NK primary paper found (PMID 41357575, 2025, IL-35 suppression of NK immunosurveillance in EGFR-mutant NSCLC) corroborates only the suppression half and does not test CD9/CD103/CD49a or ILC1-like conversion. Separately, a targeted search for a paper directly refuting in vitro NK→ILC1-like conversion as a marker artefact was run and returned zero hits — searched and not found, not "does not exist". Also noted: the paper's own sentence that the public-dataset analysis "validates the relevance of our study in vivo" is an overstatement — that section is purely in-silico re-analysis; the paper contains no in vivo experiment.
audit.downstream_dependency: Concrete and named: the ILC1-like UCell gene signature DERIVED from these IL-35-treated in vitro cultures is the instrument used to annotate the paper's merged 354,379-cell / 108-patient pan-cancer atlas (GSE131907 lung, GSE160269 esophagus, GSE166555 colon, GSE176078 breast), where the NK(T) cluster is reported to carry the highest ILC1-like enrichment score — i.e. the claim that NK cells in human tumours are IL-35-converted ILC1-like cells rests entirely on this in vitro result. That in turn underwrites the TCGA pan-cancer survival analysis stratifying patients as EBI3-high/IL12A-high/IL12B-low ("IL-35+") and reporting significantly worse overall and progression-free survival (p<0.0001 each), and the paper's closing therapeutic proposal that IL-35/IL-35R is "an attractive target for future immunotherapies aimed at enhancing NK cell clinical activity." Downstream in the field, this is the sole primary citation supporting IL-35 as an NK-plasticity driver in secondary literature, e.g. "Multidimensional plasticity of natural killer cells in tumours" (PMID 41429765, 2025). If the conversion is a TGF-β culture artefact or a reagent artefact, the tumour-relevance, prognostic, and drug-target chain all collapse; the IL-35-suppresses-NK-effector-function claim would survive independently (PMID 41357575).
audit.audit_overturns_detail: CITATION UPHELD, CLASSIFICATION OVERTURNED. The hinted citation is real and correctly attributed: Picant et al., Nat Commun 2025, PMID 40610398, is a genuine paper with Valentin Picant as first author, and it is the correct primary source for this claim. But Claude's evidence class of TRANSFER is flatly wrong and is overturned. There is NO adoptive transfer anywhere in this paper: a grep of the full archived text returns zero hits for "adoptive transfer", "congenic", "CD45.1", "NSG", "NOD scid", "humanized mouse", and "C57BL"; the only three occurrences of "in vivo" are rhetorical prose, one of them the overstated claim that in-silico public-dataset analysis "validates the relevance of our study in vivo". No cells were transferred into any recipient, there is no recipient, no congenic marker, no animal, and no in vivo timepoint — so none of the fields a TRANSFER row requires exist. The work is 100% in vitro culture of human peripheral blood NK cells, read out by surface-marker flow cytometry and scRNA-seq signature scoring. Correct strongest class is INF_INVITRO, with INF_MARKER and INF_KINETIC also present — a drop of two full tiers from the initial call. Per G7 I did not upgrade to OBS_GENETIC on the strength of the TGF-β-blockade rescue: anti-TGF-β1/2/3 antibody and Galunisertib are pharmacological/antibody blockade, not gene knockout. Per G8 the initial call was treated as a hypothesis and it did not survive the methods. One point in the paper's favour worth recording under G2: the scRNA-seq analysis uses Seurat/Harmony/Leiden clustering, UCell signature scoring, MAST differential expression and clusterProfiler only — a grep confirms NO pseudotime, RNA velocity, Monocle or Slingshot anywhere, so this claim is NOT contaminated by INF_TRAJECTORY.
audit.methods_quote: "NK cells were cultured in RPMI GlutaMAX complemented with 20% human AB Serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 1x Non-Essential Amino Acids, 1x Sodium Pyruvate (RPMI + SAB) and supplemented with IL-2 (100 UI/mL), in presence or absence of IL-35 (100 ng/mL). For blocking experiments, 10 µM Galunisertib ... or control DMSO, 10 µg/mL anti-TGFb1/2/3 ... or mouse IgG1 isotype control ... was added in the culture medium. Culture medium was renewed every 2 days for 3 to 8 days. For IL-35 starvation experiments, NK cells were washed 3 times and resuspended in RPMI + SAB supplemented with IL-2 (100UI/mL) for an additional 48 h." Also: "Healthy human blood ... was purchased anonymously from the French blood agency (Etablissement Français du sang, Lyon France, convention 16-093)." And the results text: "At day 8 in presence of IL-35 nearly all cells adopt a converted ILC1-like cell phenotype while IL-2 alone did not promote this conversion". And on survival: "NK cell survival was similar in the presence or absence of IL-35 ... even at day 9, indicating that the decreased cell number was not due to cell death."
audit.notes: Row status: claim is real and the source is correctly identified, but the evidence tier is two levels below the initial call. Precise restatement of what the evidence supports: "In vitro, recombinant single-chain IL-35 at 100 ng/mL applied to IL-2-cultured human blood NK cells from 3-5 healthy donors induces, over 2-8 days and via autocrine TGF-β, a time-dependent increase in the population frequency of CD9+CD103+CD49a+ events with reduced EOMES (T-BET unchanged), which does not reverse on IL-35 washout." It does NOT support "IL-35 drives NK toward an ILC1-like phenotype" as a lineage statement in vivo. Two specific weaknesses a reader should carry forward: (a) the causal agent measured is TGF-β, with IL-35 acting only as its inducer — blockade of TGF-β fully abolishes the effect, so attributing the differentiation to IL-35 is an attribution one step upstream of the mechanism; (b) the ILC1-like signature generated in this artificial culture is then used as the classifier on human tumour scRNA-seq, making the paper's translational section circular with respect to its own in vitro definition. Note also the incomplete transcription-factor switch (EOMES down, T-BET flat), which is not what a full NK→ILC1 lineage conversion would predict. n is small (3-5 donors) for the central marker result. Full text archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC12229632.txt.

adv.challenge_reason:
UPHELD at INF_INVITRO. I re-pulled the primary source myself (lit.py methods 40610398 --tag T6; archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC12229632.txt) and read all 14 Methods subsections verbatim rather than trusting the prior row. The Methods contain no animal section at all: "Human samples" = anonymised healthy blood from Etablissement Francais du Sang Lyon (convention 16-093), and every experimental subsection is culture (Short-term culture; Human primary NK cells sorting; Long-term culture and blocking experiment; Proliferation assay; Cytotoxic assay; Cytokine/Chemokine secretion assay; Staining and flow cytometry; scRNA-seq of cultured NK). There is no recipient, no congenic marker, no animal, no in vivo timepoint, so no OBS_TRANSFER. The auditor correctly refused OBS_GENETIC: anti-TGF-b1/2/3 (Biotechne MAB1835) and Galunisertib (Biotechne 6956) are antibody/pharmacological blockade, not gene knockout. INF_MARKER and INF_KINETIC are correctly listed as also present.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the auditor's supporting work, neither of which changes the class:
(1) The auditor asserted its greps returned "zero hits" for barcod and "no trajector anywhere". Re-running them, I get 2 hits for "barcod" and 1 for "trajector". Both are benign on inspection, so the conclusion survives, but the row overstated its own verification. "Barcoded" is CellPlex CMO sample/condition hashing ("NK cells treated with or without IL-35 were barcoded following Cell Multiplexing Oligos (CMOs) labeling protocol") — sample hashing, not lineage barcoding, so it confers no OBS_DIRECT. "Trajectories" is Discussion prose ("alternative trajectories to become ILC1-like cells"). I confirm zero hits for pseudotime/velocity/monocle/slingshot/CytoTRACE/PAGA/palantir, so G2 is genuinely not triggered and INF_TRAJECTORY is correctly absent.
(2) The auditor's what_was_measured conflates two different culture systems. The 20% human AB serum + IL-2 100 UI/mL condition is the LONG-TERM culture (which is the one supporting the marker claim, so the row is not wrong about the conversion arm); the Short-term culture is cRPMI + 10% FCS with IL-2 at 1000 UI/mL.

ONE SUBSTANTIVE OMISSION from the auditor's controls field: the paper reports "Although both cycling and non-cycling cells acquired an ILC1-like profile, the highest levels of CD9, CD103, and CD49a were observed on cycling cells." That CTV-resolved result is simultaneously the paper's best argument against pure outgrowth-selection (non-dividing cells also acquire the markers) and a signal that the effect is proliferation-associated. It belongs in the controls/alternative fields and was absent.

No genuine fate-mapping or congenic-transfer experiment was missed — none exists in this paper. No upgrade, no downgrade.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: INF_INVITRO (unchanged). Full set present: INF_INVITRO, INF_MARKER, INF_KINETIC. INF_TRAJECTORY confirmed absent (no pseudotime/RNA-velocity/Monocle/Slingshot in the Methods). No OBS_* class is supportable: no clone, cell or congenic population was ever tracked; the readout is the population frequency of CD9+CD103+CD49a+ events per well, compared paired within donor against an IL-2-alone well.
adv.new_counter_evidence:
The auditor was required (A.4) to hunt the canonical "pre-existing subset selected/expanded rather than converted" alternative and reported it as searched-and-not-found. It exists, it is directly on-target, and it carries the strongest evidence classes in the field. Three items the auditor missed:

(1) STRONGEST MISS — Flommersfeld et al., "Fate mapping of single NK cells identifies a type 1 innate lymphoid-like lineage that bridges innate and adaptive recognition of viral infection," Immunity 2021, PMID 34437840 / PMC8528403 (full text already archived locally as /home/user/aaa/refs/D2_PMC8528403.txt). Methods: retroviral fluorescent colour-barcoding of HSCs, retrogenic mice, sorting of SINGLE colour-barcoded CD27+Ly49H+ NK cells, multiplexed adoptive transfer into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- / Klra8-/- / NKp46iCre x R26-LSL-iDTA recipients, serial re-transfer into secondary hosts, plus CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic PARABIOSIS. This is OBS_DIRECT + OBS_TRANSFER class, and it instantiates exactly the alternative: (a) ILC1-like NK cells derive from a PRE-EXISTING, prospectively sortable steady-state CD27+CD62L- subset — single cells sorted from that compartment "exclusively generated CD62L- clones"; (b) section heading "ILC1-like NK cells do not serve as precursors of CD62L+ NK cells" — the two are separate lineages that retain distinct phenotypes through the memory phase and upon reinfection; (c) parabiosis: ILC1-like NK cells "remained almost entirely spleen resident, while cNK cells equilibrated between the two parabionts"; (d) the authors re-analysed HUMAN NK scRNA-seq and found the same bifurcation into two lineages by mutually exclusive CD160/XCL1 vs GZMB. So the tissue-resident ILC1-like group-1 ILC phenotype maps onto a pre-existing lineage, not a conversion endpoint.

(2) The field's own flagship in vivo conversion paper concedes the definitive assays FAILED. Park et al., "Toxoplasma gondii infection drives conversion of NK cells into ILC1-like cells," eLife 2019, PMID 31393266 / PMC6703900 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC6703900.txt), states verbatim: "an Eomes fate-mapping mouse, that is, EomesCre, could be used to identify a cell-intrinsic role for Eomes, this was not possible due to the ubiquitous expression of Eomes during development (data not shown)" and "Another approach would be to examine Eomes downregulation following adoptive transfer of congenic NK cells prior to infection but this was hindered due to the inability to find transferred cells after 14 d.p.i. (data not shown)." They retreated to Ncr1iCre Eomes-fl/fl mixed BM chimeras. Consequences: NK-to-ILC1 conversion has never been established by OBS_DIRECT anywhere, and their own data show a pre-existing Eomes-INDEPENDENT CD49a+ ILC1 pool that expands on infection ("mild ILC1 expansion occurs in the absence of NK cells") — i.e. part of the ILC1-like pool is selected/expanded, not converted. Also in tension with Picant: "culture of purified NK cells from infected mice did not result in Eomes downregulation," implying cell-extrinsic requirements absent from Picant's purified-NK culture.

(3) Sojka et al., eLife 2014, PMID 24714492 — parabiosis plus transcription-factor-deficient mice show liver/uterine/skin CD49a+DX5- tissue-resident NK are cell lineages DISTINCT from conventional splenic and thymic NK. CD49a+ group-1 ILCs have an independent developmental origin, so detecting CD49a+ cells does not license an ex-NK inference.

REPLICATION CHECK (I ran it properly rather than relying on a keyword query): Europe PMC citations endpoint MED/40610398/citations returned hitCount=12; I read all 12 titles. No replication, no dispute, no failed reproduction. The only primary IL-35/NK paper among them (PMID 41357575) corroborates the suppression half only. This upholds the auditor's strand 3.

I also independently confirm the auditor's other two strands are fairly stated: the reagent-validity caveat (Aparicio-Siegmund, PLoS One 2014, PMID 25259790) and the mechanistic displacement onto autocrine TGF-b (blockade abolishes the effect; TGF-b alone reproduces it; upstream primaries Gao PMID 28759001, Cortez PMID 27156386). One caveat on the auditor's wording: it described Gao et al. 2017 as "with genetic fate mapping." Gao is paywalled (lit.py returns ABSTRACT_ONLY, no PMCID); the abstract describes "global transcriptomic and flow-cytometry analyses and genetically engineered mouse models" and does not mention fate mapping. I could not obtain the Gao Methods, so I cannot verify the fate-mapping characterisation and flag it as unsupported rather than false.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
The invoked general process is TGF-b-driven acquisition of tissue-residency integrins on a circulating lymphocyte. I searched the TRM, ILC and myeloid literatures. All three bear directly, and two of them supply a methodological verdict on the exact assay Picant used.

T CELL / TRM — decisive. Zitti et al., Immunity 2023, PMID 37269830 is the precise methodological analogue and it is damaging to Picant's inference. In vitro stimulation of CIRCULATING human blood CD8+CD45RA-CD62L+ T cells with IL-15 + TGF-b induced CD49a and a cytotoxic TRM transcriptional profile, RUNX2- and RUNX3-dependent. Two lessons. First, TGF-b induction of CD49a/CD103 on circulating human lymphocytes is a generic, cross-lineage program — it is not diagnostic of any lineage, so CD9/CD103/CD49a acquisition cannot by itself mean "ILC1." Second and more important: the T cell field did NOT stop at marker induction. It established the precursor-product relationship by TCR CLONAL REPERTOIRE OVERLAP between PAIRED skin and blood samples from the same donors. That clonal step is exactly what converts marker induction into a lineage claim, and it is exactly what Picant lacks. NK cells carry no rearranged receptor, so the clonal shortcut is unavailable to them — which is precisely why the NK field must use retroviral barcoding or congenic transfer (as Flommersfeld PMID 34437840 did) and why a population-frequency comparison between wells is the weakest available design. Note the sting: RUNX2 sits in Picant's own IL-35-upregulated DEG list, alongside ITGA1, ITGAE, CD9, CXCR3/4 — i.e. what Picant labels an "ILC1-like" program is the RUNX-driven TGF-b residency program shared with CD8 TRM, not an ILC1 lineage program.
Corroborating, same field: Girard et al., Mucosal Immunol 2024, PMID 38729611 — MAdCAM-1 + retinoic acid + TGF-b induces blood CD8 T cells to express CD103, CD69, CD101, CCR5, CCR9 and a4b7; the authors frame this explicitly as a "TRM-LIKE phenotype" and "a means to expand these cells in vitro," i.e. a phenotype-induction protocol, never a lineage conversion. Mackay et al., Nat Immunol 2013, doi 10.1038/ni.2744 — CD103 on skin TRM requires local IL-15 + TGF-b AFTER epithelial entry; residency markers are microenvironment-imposed, not cell-autonomous identity. Fonseca et al., Nat Immunol 2020, PMID 32066954 — TRM are not terminally committed: reactivated TRM rejoin the circulating pool and ex-TRM redifferentiate into TCM and TEM. This directly undercuts Picant's headline word "irreversible," which rests on a 48-hour washout during which the cells were still producing autocrine TGF-b; the home field shows this class of differentiation state reverses over weeks, not hours. Fung et al., Sci Immunol 2022, PMID 36332012 — CD103 fate mapping shows CD103 expression is itself dynamic and CD103- TRM are the primary responders; CD103 is a fluctuating state marker, not a stable lineage label.

ILC. Gasteiger et al., Science 2015, PMID 26472762 — parabiosis shows ILCs in lymphoid and non-lymphoid organs are tissue-resident, maintained and expanded LOCALLY by self-renewal, with only partial hematogenous replenishment late after infection. Tissue ILC1 pools are largely self-sustaining, so intratumoral ILC1-like cells need not be ex-NK.

MYELOID — the cautionary precedent, and the single most instructive one. Ginhoux et al., Science 2010, PMID 20966214 and Hashimoto et al., Immunity 2013, PMID 23601688. The "circulating monocytes convert into tissue-resident macrophages" model stood as dogma for decades on precisely this evidence structure: marker similarity plus in vitro differentiation of blood monocytes into macrophage-like cells bearing tissue-macrophage markers. Parabiosis and genetic fate mapping overturned it. Hashimoto's own framing: "Despite accumulating evidence suggesting local self-maintenance of tissue macrophages in the steady state, the dogma remains that tissue macrophages derive from monocytes. Using parabiosis and fate-mapping approaches, we confirmed that monocytes do not show significant contribution to tissue macrophages in the steady state." The resident population turned out to be pre-existing, embryonically derived and locally self-renewing, and the in vitro "monocyte-derived macrophage" was a culture phenotype that did not correspond to the in vivo resident cell. That is the exact structural risk in T6, stated by the field that already made the mistake.

METHODOLOGICAL VERDICT these fields deliver on the assays used here: bulk population-frequency shifts + residency-integrin flow markers + a self-derived UCell signature cannot discriminate conversion from selection, nor from a reversible TGF-b state. The assays that CAN discriminate — parabiosis, congenic transfer, genetic fate mapping, clonal repertoire overlap, and in humans transplant chimerism plus intravascular labelling — are all established. Critically, the human NK toolkit demonstrably exists: Buggert/Bjorkstrom et al., "Transient tissue residency and lymphatic egress define human CD56bright NK cell homeostasis," Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907, used intravascular labelling, human LIVER TRANSPLANT donor-versus-recipient chimerism, humanized mice, non-human primates and efferent lymph fluid cannulation to show that infiltrating recipient NK cells acquire tissue-residency traits in vivo (partly Runx3-regulated) and that human NK residency is TRANSIENT with lymphatic recirculation. That paper simultaneously (i) supports that circulating human NK CAN acquire residency traits in vivo, (ii) contradicts "irreversible," and (iii) sets the standard of evidence Picant did not attempt.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
The auditor said MEDIUM. I downgrade to LOW, while keeping and sharpening its named dependency.

CONCRETE NAMED DOWNSTREAM DEPENDENCY (retained, and shown to be weaker than the auditor thought): the ILC1-like UCell signature derived from these IL-35-treated in vitro cultures is the classifier applied to the merged 354,379-cell / 108-patient pan-cancer atlas (GSE131907 lung, GSE160269 esophagus, GSE166555 colon, GSE176078 breast). The load-bearing sentence is explicit and self-referential: "the NK(T) cluster displayed the highest enrichment score for our ILC1-like gene signature, as defined by scRNA-seq analysis of IL-35-exposed NK cells." That single inference carries the TCGA pan-cancer survival analysis (patients stratified IL12A+EBI3+IL12B- as "IL-35", p<0.0001 for OS and PFS) and the closing proposal of IL-35/IL-35R as an immunotherapy target.

DEFECT THE AUDITOR MISSED, and it is the decisive one: the annotated cluster is "NK(T)" — a MERGED NK-plus-T-cell cluster, per the paper's own harmonised cell-type annotation. The signature's defining genes (ITGA1, ITGAE, CD9, CXCR3/4, RUNX2) are the canonical human CD8 TRM program — ITGA1/CD49a and RUNX2 specifically established as such in human skin TRM by Zitti et al., Immunity 2023, PMID 37269830. Scoring a generic TGF-b/tissue-residency signature on a cluster that by construction contains T cells cannot distinguish IL-35-converted NK cells from ordinary CD8 TRM. So the paper's one translational inference is not merely circular with its own in vitro definition (the auditor's point) — it is also not cell-type-resolved. Both failure modes have to hold for the chain to stand.

WHY LOW RATHER THAN MEDIUM:
(1) Field uptake is negligible and non-experimental. Europe PMC forward citations = 12 in roughly 13 months (I read all 12). Zero replications, zero primary studies building experimentally on the conversion. The reviews that cite it (PMID 41429765 "Multidimensional plasticity of natural killer cells in tumours"; PMID 41405717) list it as one example among many in NK plasticity, not as a foundation. The auditor's own note that this is "the sole primary citation supporting IL-35 as an NK-plasticity driver in secondary literature" describes citation in a review, which is not load-bearing in the sense A.5 requires.
(2) The mechanistic content is fully displaced onto TGF-b and is independently owned elsewhere. Blockade with anti-TGF-b1/2/3 or Galunisertib abolishes the phenotype; TGF-b alone reproduces it. TGF-b-driven NK-to-ILC1-like conversion was already established by Gao PMID 28759001 and Cortez PMID 27156386. Delete the IL-35 attribution and nothing downstream in the field moves.
(3) The claim is severable from the paper's robust half. The IL-35-suppresses-NK-effector-function finding stands independently and is separately corroborated (PMID 41357575, EGFR-mutant NSCLC), so a collapse of the conversion claim does not take the paper's replicated content with it.
Net: this claim currently bears load only inside its own paper — intra-paper load, not field load. That is LOW.
adv.better_primary_source:
For the IL-35-SPECIFIC claim as worded, there is no better primary source and none is needed: Picant V, Revol-Bauz L, Tonon L, et al. "Interleukin-35 impairs human NK cell effector functions and induces their ILC1-like conversion with tissue residency features." Nat Commun. 2025 Jul 3;16:4782. PMID 40610398; PMCID PMC12229632; DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-61196-0 (preprint Res Sq 10.21203/rs.3.rs-4030216/v1, 2024). I independently verified authorship, journal, year and PMCID, and pulled the full text (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC12229632.txt). It is the first and only primary source for the IL-35 version. The auditor's citation call is UPHELD.

However, the row should carry three pointers, because the claim as worded is one causal step upstream of what was actually measured:
(1) For the mechanism that was actually measured — TGF-b-driven NK to CD49a+CD103+CD9+ ILC1-like conversion — the stronger and prior primary sources are Gao Y et al., Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004-1015, PMID 28759001 (mouse, in vivo tumour models; NOTE: paywalled, ABSTRACT_ONLY via lit.py, no PMCID — I could NOT read its Methods, so the auditor's "with genetic fate mapping" description is UNVERIFIED and should not be relied on), and Cortez VS et al., PMID 27156386.
(2) For the strongest-methodology primary source in this problem space overall — which reaches the OPPOSITE conclusion and which the auditor missed entirely — Flommersfeld S et al., Immunity 2021;54:2288-2304, PMID 34437840, PMCID PMC8528403. Single-cell retroviral colour-barcoding, multiplexed single-cell adoptive transfer, serial re-transfer and congenic parabiosis establish that ILC1-like NK cells are a separate, pre-existing lineage rather than a conversion product. Full text already archived locally at /home/user/aaa/refs/D2_PMC8528403.txt.
(3) For the human in vivo standard of evidence this claim would need to meet — Buggert M / Bjorkstrom NK et al., Nat Immunol 2025;26:2004-2015, PMID 41087727, PMCID PMC12571907, which used human liver-transplant donor/recipient chimerism, intravascular labelling and efferent lymph cannulation to track human NK residency acquisition in vivo, and found that residency is TRANSIENT.

Precise restatement of what the T6 evidence actually supports: "In vitro, recombinant single-chain IL-35 at 100 ng/mL added to IL-2-cultured human blood NK cells from 3-5 healthy donors increases, over 2-8 days and via autocrine TGF-b, the population frequency of CD9+CD103+CD49a+ events, with reduced EOMES and unchanged T-BET, and this does not reverse within a 48-hour washout." It does NOT support a lineage statement, and it does not support the in vivo/tumour claim.
